claims.text: The as-synthesized nanoscale PtPdRhRuIrOs catalyst has a homogeneous, random atomic distribution with no significant short-range order.
Annealing at approximately 400 °C will induce limited short-range atomic ordering in nanoscale PtPdRhRuIrOs.
The proposed annealing treatment can induce short-range ordering without causing phase segregation.
Short-range atomic order can coexist with an overall solid-solution nanoparticle structure lacking elemental segregation or intermetallic phases.
The annealed PtPdRhRuIrOs catalyst will form short-range atomic clusters or local compositional ordering.
The local ordering will preferentially cluster similar atoms.
Short-range ordering modifies the local electronic structure of catalytic active sites, potentially including shifts in their d-band centers.
The ordering-induced electronic changes optimize adsorption energies for key ethanol-oxidation intermediates.
Optimized intermediate adsorption energies improve ethanol-oxidation kinetics.
The ordering-induced changes reduce catalyst deactivation pathways.
The annealed catalyst will have higher ethanol-oxidation activity than the as-synthesized catalyst.
The annealed catalyst will have greater operational durability than the as-synthesized catalyst.
Performance changes will include altered onset potentials, increased current densities, and improved operational stability.
The hypothesized benefit is expected only when ordering occurs without phase separation and ethanol oxidation is operated between 25 and 80 °C.
EXAFS or atom-probe tomography can be used to compare short-range ordering between the annealed and baseline catalysts.
Failure to observe improved ethanol-oxidation performance despite a statistically significant increase in short-range ordering would falsify the proposed ordering-performance relationship.
